evidence.why: A real sanitiser (DOMPurify) with an explicit tag/attribute allowlist is applied to the SVG content before it is written to disk and served back.
Filename used to build the file path is restricted to a safe character set, mitigating path traversal on the serving surface.

controls_present: DOMPurify sanitisation with explicit ALLOWED_TAGS/ALLOWED_ATTR allowlist for SVG
filename character allowlist before path join
content-type validated on upload and serve
structured logging (console.log with object, not string concatenation)
other_classes_observed: Import `import { DOMPurify } from 'dompurify'` is not the correct named export for dompurify, which could cause a runtime error rather than silently skipping sanitisation

CSP header in next.config.js is scoped to /api/avatar/:path* but the avatar URL returned to clients points to /uploads/... (a static public asset path), so the CSP may not actually apply to the served SVG
Avatar GET route (snippet_03.ts) has no authorization/ownership check, allowing any user to fetch any other user's avatar by guessing userId/fileName
